title: Nutty German Chicken Casserole
description: A peppery and gooey German dish featuring chicken stock concentrate and lacquer-glaze, perfect for a crowd, this low-glycemic-friendly casserole is a delight to eat. It combines the richness of chicken and nuts with a sweet and tangy lacquer-glaze.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat and cook the chicken until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
In a separate saucepan, combine the chicken stock concentrate, lacquer-glaze, and heavy cream, and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked chicken, sliced almonds, black pepper, and salt, and stir until well combined.
Pour the cream mixture over the chicken mixture and stir until the chicken is well coated.
Transfer the mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish and top with shredded cheese.
Dot the top of the casserole with the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter.
Bake the casserole in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove the casserole from the oven and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Let the casserole rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
